answers: Who keeps it: Model / Frontier labs
counterevidence: The ledger holds what parties and filings confirm, so quiet deals are missed until they surface, and acquihires surface late; a rise can reflect how thoroughly a quarter was searched. Many deals are small team hires that say little about margins, and one buyer's spree (OpenAI's) moves the count on its own.
definition: Deals in the trailing four quarters by which an AI lab or a compute company took a company in the layers above the model layer (training input, serving and orchestration, deployment and application), by purchase, acquihire, or a licence or stake that came with its leaders; derived metric lab_vertical_integration_events_4q over the acquisition ledger (acq.<acquirer>.<target>.pt rows, each with a fetched announcement), searched under a written rule and read only for quarters a search has covered.

direction_rule.rationale: Four quarters. A yearly count of rare events varies between two years with no trend by about the square root of twice its level, which at the December 2025 count after the September 2026 search is about seven, so a smaller move is stable. More deals per year concentrate the application layer into the labs.

timing_rationale: Leading: an acquisition is announced before the acquired layer's economics change, so the count moves ahead of margins.
tracker_interpretation: A search of every counted buyer's deals since January 2025, under a rule written down first, more than tripled the count in September 2026: the labs, OpenAI above all, and the compute companies are taking coding tools, evaluation and inference software, agents and consumer apps at a steady clip since late 2025, after a slower first half of 2025. The trailing year is read only from the end of 2025, and the direction rule waits for five quarters a search has covered.
why_it_matters: The application layer's exit bell. When the labs buy the layer above them, the surplus that layer was capturing moves down the stack; a rising count is the capture thesis's clearest leading signal.
